proposal: The chapter recommends repealing the tax increases from the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act (book minimum tax, stock buyback excise tax, coal excise tax, Superfund tax, drug-manufacturer excise tax) and the green-energy credits in its Subtitle D. It also recommends making the 2017 increase in the estate and gift tax exemption permanent, fully repealing the state and local tax deduction, and cutting the tax on global intangible low-taxed income to no more than 12.5 percent.

status_summary: Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) set the estate and gift tax basic exclusion at 15 million dollars for decedents dying and gifts made after 2025-12-31, indexed for inflation for decedents dying after 2026, and ended or phased out many Inflation Reduction Act energy credits: per the amended U.S. Code, the clean vehicle credit (30D) ended for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30, the home energy efficiency and residential clean energy credits (25C and 25D) ended after 2025-12-31, wind and solar facilities whose construction begins after 2026-07-04 lose the production and investment credits (45Y and 48E) if placed in service after 2027, and the advanced manufacturing credit (45X) ends for wind components after 2027 and metallurgical coal after 2029 with critical minerals phased out after 2033, while the clean fuel credit (45Z) was extended through 2029 and, per law-firm summaries, the carbon capture and nuclear credits (45Q and 45U) continue with new foreign-entity restrictions. The deduction for net CFC tested income (formerly global intangible low-taxed income) is now 40 percent, which at the 21 percent corporate rate implies an effective rate of about 12.6 percent (an inference), close to the chapter's 12.5 percent ceiling, and a law-firm summary reports the foreign tax credit haircut cut from 20 to 10 percent. On the state and local tax deduction the Act moved opposite to the chapter in the near term, setting the cap at 40,000 dollars for 2025 and 40,400 dollars for 2026, then 101 percent of the prior year through 2029 with a phase-down for high incomes, and 10,000 dollars after 2029, instead of repealing the deduction. Per the Code amendment notes, the Act did not repeal the 1 percent stock buyback excise tax and kept the corporate book minimum tax, changing only its depreciation and intangible drilling cost adjustments (section 70523), and it set the base erosion tax rate at 10.5 percent.

uncertainties: The official enrolled text of Title VII was not readable on govinfo.gov (the copy opened on 2026-10-22 ends in the first title, at section 10507); the enacted provisions were checked on 2026-10-22 through the amendment notes of the U.S. Code reproductions hosted by law.cornell.edu, which are not the official publication. Read and matching: 26 U.S.C. 2010 (basic exclusion 15 million dollars, indexed for decedents dying after 2026, section 70106, 139 Stat. 162, applying after 2025-12-31); 164 (cap 40,000 dollars for 2025, 40,400 for 2026, 101 percent of the prior year through 2029, 10,000 after 2029, income phase-down, section 70120, 139 Stat. 169); 250 (33.34 and 40 percent, sections 70321 to 70323); 59A (10.5 percent, section 70331); 56A (section 70523, 139 Stat. 281); 25C, 25D, 30D, 45X, 45Y, 45Z and 48E (end dates and extensions). The 1 percent rate in 26 U.S.C. 4501 shows no note from the 2025 law, but that finding rests on the absence of a note on a host whose other pages do show the 2025 law, not on a statement; the same applies to the unchanged 15 percent book minimum tax rate in section 55, whose page was not opened. The 12.6 percent effective rate follows from the 40 percent deduction and the 21 percent corporate rate and is not a stated figure. Not checked against the Code notes: the foreign tax credit haircut change, the 25E and 45W end dates (both resting on the Pierce Atwood and Ropes & Gray summaries), the continuation of 45Q and 45U (resting on those summaries and an external retrieval), and the coal excise tax, the Superfund tax and the drug manufacturer excise tax. The base erosion tax, which the same chapter page asks to eliminate, was set at 10.5 percent rather than repealed; it is outside this record's proposal. Treasury guidance on the credits issued in 2026 was not checked. The Pierce Atwood alert's publication day is approximate (July 2025).
